issues.failure_explanation: The assumptions control the form with stabilisation coefficient one, but never require nonnegative stabilisation. They therefore do not imply coercivity for arbitrary positive tau_0. For example, on a fitted Q0 mesh let P average over adjacent-cell pairs and set s(r,q)=-a((I-P)r,(I-P)q), with 0<a<1. This satisfies the diagonal equivalence, vanishes on constants, and has the required first-order weak consistency. At tau_0=1/a, however, the stabilised projection is singular on ker(P). The uniqueness used by the lemma is consequently unestablished. The same omission affects the flux coercivity argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: {The interpolation estimates for $u$, $\dv{u}$ and $p$, together with the trace inequality for the boundary term in $\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{d},h}$ and Assumption~\ref{as:extensions}, then prove the theorem.}

issues.failure_explanation: The trace inequality gives h^{-1} times the squared normal-trace interpolation error of order h^{2r-2}, not h^{2r}, from H^r regularity. There is also a direct smooth counterexample: on a fitted unit square with RT0 elements and pure flux boundaries, take u=(0,x), p=0 and g=0. Every discrete normal trace on a horizontal boundary edge is constant, so its best boundary L2 error is at least c h. The penalty contribution therefore makes the flux norm error at least c sqrt(h), whereas the claimed right-hand side gives O(h) with r=1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain the proved best-approximation bound with its explicit h^{-1/2}-weighted normal-trace error, and state the resulting weaker boundary-dependent rates and regularity requirements. issues.failure_explanation: The assumed L2-bounded commuting interpolator is not assumed cellwise local. Canonical cellwise RT/BDM interpolation uses face moments and is not L2-bounded; bounded commuting projections generally use neighbouring cells. The proof combines these incompatible properties to obtain its local L2 bound. Its subtraction of aggregate-wise polynomials through the conforming interpolator is likewise unjustified when those polynomials have normal jumps between aggregates.
